Single file written; nothing else under /output touched. Zero imports (uses only ambient Date/Math), no node: builtins, no require/module.exports, no crypto/Buffer/TextEncoder references anywhere (grep-verified).

API:
- timeTime() -> float seconds since epoch = Date.now()/1000 (ms resolution; Python's clock has us resolution, immaterial once truncated to whole seconds).
- pyInt(value) -> integral Number. Truncates toward zero via Math.trunc (int(-1.9) === -1, NOT -2). Also accepts booleans (int(True)===1, bool subclasses int in Python) and base-10 decimal strings with surrounding whitespace, optional +/- sign and PEP 515 underscore separators ('1_000' -> 1000). String support was added because python-jose's claim validators call int(claims['exp'])/int(claims['iat']) on possibly-string values inside try/except ValueError, so jwt.mjs can reuse this directly.
- nowEpochSeconds() -> pyInt(timeTime()), i.e. the exact `int(time.time())` value for the iat claim.

Error behaviour (relevant to jwt.mjs claim validation): pyInt throws real Error objects whose .name mirrors the Python exception type, carrying Python's exact message text, so callers can branch on err.name instead of string-matching:
- NaN         -> name 'ValueError',    'cannot convert float NaN to integer'
- +/-Infinity -> name 'OverflowError', 'cannot convert float infinity to integer'
- bad string  -> name 'ValueError',    "invalid literal for int() with base 10: '<original untrimmed text>'"
- other types -> name 'TypeError',     "int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not '<pytype>'" (null/undefined -> 'NoneType', Array -> 'list', Map -> 'dict')
Note: python-jose's iat/exp validators catch ValueError only, so if you need that narrow catch, test err.name === 'ValueError'.

Intentional limitations, documented in comments: no arbitrary-precision integers (values beyond 2^53 lose exactness, irrelevant for epoch seconds), and string parsing accepts ASCII digits only (Python also accepts other Unicode Nd digits).

Verification: /workspace/verify/pytime-verify.mjs (33 assertions, ALL PASS, exit 0) covers truncation direction, -0, booleans, string forms, and all four error names/messages. Cross-checked against the reference: /workspace/dataset/test17_executable --data cross --verify_iat true printed iat 1786341868 while nowEpochSeconds() returned 1786341868 in the same second (also matches `date +%s`).

Exactly one file written: /output/lib/bytes.mjs. No other /output file created or modified. Zero imports of any kind (no relative, no builtin) — the module is fully standalone. Grep-clean for crypto/subtle/createHmac/createHash/Buffer/TextEncoder/TextDecoder/require(/module.exports, including in comments and strings.

SIGNATURES (exactly as specified in the module layout):
- utf8Encode(str) -> Uint8Array. Coerces non-strings via String(). ASCII 1 byte, <=U+07FF 2 bytes, <=U+FFFF 3 bytes, well-formed surrogate pair -> single 4-byte astral sequence. An unpaired surrogate (lone high, or low with no preceding high) emits the three bytes ef bf bd (U+FFFD) — never CESU-8.
- utf8Decode(bytes) -> string. Accepts Uint8Array or number[] (null/undefined -> ''). Emits exactly one U+FFFD per maximal ill-formed subsequence, matching the WHATWG replacement policy bit for bit. Rejects: stray continuations 0x80-0xBF, invalid leads 0xC0/0xC1/0xF5-0xFF, overlong forms (via narrowed second-byte bounds: 0xE0 needs 0xA0-0xBF, 0xF0 needs 0x90-0xBF), 3-byte-encoded surrogates (0xED capped at 0x9F), code points above U+10FFFF (0xF4 capped at 0x8F), and truncated sequences including one cut off at end-of-input. IMPORTANT for callers: an invalid continuation byte is NOT consumed — it is re-examined as a lead byte, so [0xE0,0x41] decodes to "�A", not "�". Astral code points are re-split into surrogate pairs on output.
- latin1Encode(str) -> Uint8Array. Low byte of each UTF-16 code unit (charCodeAt & 0xff). Lossy by design for code units > 0xFF — intended for base64 intermediates / raw byte-in-string material only, NOT for text.
- concatBytes(list) -> Uint8Array. Accepts an array of Uint8Array or number[] entries; tolerates null/undefined for the list and for individual entries. Always returns a fresh array (never aliases an input).
- bytesEqual(a, b) -> boolean. Length-then-content compare, EARLY-RETURN and therefore NOT timing-safe. Signature/MAC comparison must use constantTimeEqual from hmac.mjs instead; a doc comment in the file points there.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL the integrator may care about: utf8Decode accumulates UTF-16 code units and flushes through String.fromCharCode.apply every 4096 units (module-private STRING_CHUNK_SIZE), joining chunks at the end. This bounds the apply() argument list so arbitrarily long inputs cannot overflow the call stack. Verified on a 15,000-code-unit input.

VERIFICATION (scratch harness /workspace/verify/bytes_mjs_check.mjs, run with node v18.19.1, output "ALL BYTES CHECKS PASSED"):
- Encoder matched the platform reference codec on a 22-case corpus (ASCII, 2/3/4-byte, U+10FFFF, lone high/low surrogates, 'high surrogate followed by a valid pair') plus 3,000 random-string fuzz cases.
- Decoder matched the WHATWG reference decoder on 34 hand-picked malformed sequences plus 5,000 uniform-random byte-string fuzz cases plus 20,000 biased-alphabet fuzz cases drawn from a near-valid lead/continuation pool. Zero mismatches across all ~28,000 cases.
- Cross-checked against the reference executable: for --data '中文测试' --verify_iat true, the live token's payload segment decodes via utf8Decode to {"info":"中文测试","iat":1786341922} and re-encodes via utf8Encode to byte-identical output; same for the header segment {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}.
- latin1Encode, concatBytes (including empty list and number[] entries), and bytesEqual (equal, differing length, differing byte, both empty) covered by unit assertions.

NOTE ON SCOPE: the Python script's payload JSON is ensure_ascii=True, so in the happy path utf8Encode only ever sees ASCII (header JSON, payload JSON, the "secret" key, the signing input). The full non-ASCII and malformed-input handling above is there so base64url.mjs / pyjson.mjs / jws.mjs can rely on it unconditionally. Only /output/lib/errors.mjs was created; nothing else under /output was touched. Zero imports (no relative, no node: builtins), no crypto/Buffer/TextEncoder/TextDecoder references, no `require(`/`module.exports` anywhere including comments and strings. 177 lines, pure ESM.

HIERARCHY (matches jose/exceptions.py):
  Error <- JOSEError <- JWSError <- {JWSSignatureError, JWSAlgorithmError}
                     <- JWTError <- {JWTClaimsError, ExpiredSignatureError}
                     <- JWKError
Every constructor is `constructor(message)` (message optional), calls super, and sets this.name to its own class-name string literal (e.g. new JWTClaimsError().name === 'JWTClaimsError'). Base constructor also calls Error.captureStackTrace when available, so the error's own constructor frames are trimmed from .stack.

STATIC DEFAULT MESSAGES — each class exposes a static DEFAULT_MESSAGE used only when the constructor gets undefined/null. Resolution uses new.target, so a subclass default wins:
  JOSEError.DEFAULT_MESSAGE          = ''    (inherited by JWSError, JWTError, JWTClaimsError, JWKError)
  JWSSignatureError.DEFAULT_MESSAGE  = 'Signature verification failed.'
  JWSAlgorithmError.DEFAULT_MESSAGE  = 'Algorithm not supported.'
  ExpiredSignatureError.DEFAULT_MESSAGE = 'Signature has expired.'
So `new JWSAlgorithmError()` already carries 'Algorithm not supported.'; jws.mjs may pass the string explicitly too — either way the message is identical.

MESSAGE COERCION (module-local normalizeMessage, not exported):
  undefined / null -> the class DEFAULT_MESSAGE ('' for most), mirroring Python's `raise JWSError` with no args
  an Error instance -> its .message, mirroring python-jose's `raise JWSError(e)` where str(e) is what surfaces
  '' (empty string) -> kept as '' (NOT replaced by the default)
  anything else -> String(value)

FOR INTEGRATORS: jwt.mjs/jws.mjs should pass their exact python-jose wording as the argument, e.g. new JWTClaimsError('Issued At claim (iat) must be an integer.'), new JWSError('Not enough segments'), new JWSError('The specified alg value is not allowed'). Nothing in this module prints anything or touches process. JWKError is an extra export beyond the spec list, added for hierarchy fidelity with python-jose; it is purely additive and no other module needs to import it. All spec-listed names are present and spelled exactly as required.

Implements RFC 2104 HMAC-SHA256 on top of ./sha256.mjs. No platform primitives, no builtin modules, no forbidden identifiers (verified by a case-insensitive scan for require(, module.exports, crypto, subtle, webcrypto, createHmac, createHash, Buffer, TextEncoder, TextDecoder, node: -> CLEAN). ESM only, .mjs imports carry explicit suffixes. node --check passes.

IMPORTS (both relative, .mjs suffixed):
- './sha256.mjs': sha256, SHA256_BLOCK_SIZE, SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE
- './bytes.mjs': utf8Encode
bytes.mjs has landed and exports utf8Encode (confirmed). sha256.mjs did NOT exist yet while I worked, so those three imports are written strictly to the published interface spec and need a link check once that file lands.

API CONTRACT:
- hmacSha256(keyBytes, messageBytes) -> Uint8Array(32). Both args accept either a Uint8Array or a string; strings are UTF-8 encoded via utf8Encode (python-jose accepts str keys), so hmacSha256('secret', signingInput) === hmacSha256(utf8Encode('secret'), utf8Encode(signingInput)). Anything else throws TypeError. Inputs are never mutated. Keys > 64 bytes are pre-hashed, shorter keys zero-padded; ipad 0x36 / opad 0x5c.
- constantTimeEqual(a, b) -> boolean. Length is checked first (matching Python hmac.compare_digest, which also short-circuits on length), then an accumulating XOR over all bytes. NOTE FOR jws.mjs: it returns false (does not throw) for non-Uint8Array args, so pass real byte arrays -- handing it a base64 string would silently fail the signature check.

Only file written under /output: /output/lib/base64url.mjs. Sole import is `import { utf8Encode } from './bytes.mjs';` (explicit .mjs, relative). No node: builtins, no crypto/Web Crypto/Buffer/TextEncoder/atob-btoa references anywhere (verified with a case-insensitive grep that now returns zero matches — even the word "buffer" was removed from comments to keep naive scanners quiet). No `require(` / `module.exports`.

API details the integrator should know:

1) base64UrlEncode(bytes) -> string. Accepts a Uint8Array or a plain number[]. Unpadded, "-_" alphabet, built with the classic 3-byte -> 4-char shift grouping; the 1-/2-byte tail emits 2/3 chars and NO "=" is ever produced. Output is assembled in 4096-char chunks then joined, so a 200 KB input is fine.

2) base64UrlDecode(str) -> Uint8Array. Lenient exactly where python-jose is:
   - any amount of missing padding is accepted (length implies it);
   - trailing "=" padding, if present, is stripped and ignored (including the degenerate "====" -> empty);
   - BOTH alphabets decode: "-"/"_" and "+"/"/" map to 62/63;
   - non-canonical surplus low bits in the final character are discarded rather than rejected (matches Python's base64.b64decode).
   Strict elsewhere: ANY other character (space, newline, ".", an inner "=", non-ASCII) throws, and `end % 4 === 1` throws ("length leaves a single trailing character") since no encoder can produce it. It also accepts a Uint8Array/number[] of ASCII char codes, which is handy if jws.mjs splits the token as bytes rather than as a string.

3) Errors are plain `Error` instances (messages: "Invalid base64url character: 'X'" / "U+000a" style, and "Invalid base64url string: length leaves a single trailing character."). I deliberately did NOT import errors.mjs — that would add a dependency and an export outside the fixed interface — so jws.mjs should wrap these itself, e.g. catch around the header/claims decode and re-raise JWSError('Invalid header padding') / ('Invalid crypto padding') in python-jose wording.

4) base64UrlEncodeText(str) = base64UrlEncode(utf8Encode(str)), so astral chars go through bytes.mjs' 4-byte path and lone surrogates become U+FFFD, per that module's contract.

Exactly one file written: /output/lib/sha256.mjs. No other file under /output was created or modified.

INTERFACE (matches the spec exactly, no extra exports):
  export const SHA256_BLOCK_SIZE = 64
  export const SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE = 32
  export function sha256(input) -> Uint8Array(32)

IMPORTS: only `import { utf8Encode } from './bytes.mjs';` (the one optional dependency allowed). bytes.mjs itself imports nothing, so there is no cycle. If a future refactor wants sha256.mjs fully standalone, deleting that import and the `typeof input === 'string'` branch in toMessageBytes() is the only change needed.

INPUT HANDLING: sha256() accepts Uint8Array (fast path, zero-copy, input never mutated), string (UTF-8 encoded via utf8Encode first — convenience for an at_hash-style caller), ArrayBuffer, and number[]. Anything else throws TypeError('sha256 expects a Uint8Array or a string'). hmac.mjs already passes Uint8Array only, so nothing changes for it.

IMPLEMENTATION: FIPS 180-4 from scratch — the 64 K constants, H(0) initial values, ROTR/Ch/Maj/BigSigma0/BigSigma1/smallSigma0/smallSigma1 as small named functions, 64-word message schedule, 64-round compression loop, every intermediate coerced with `>>> 0`. Padding writes 0x80, zeros, then a 64-bit big-endian bit length whose high word is Math.floor(len / 536870912) (= len*8 / 2^32) and low word (len*8) >>> 0, so messages over 512 MiB still pad correctly. Complete blocks are compressed straight out of the caller's buffer; only the 64- or 128-byte padded tail is allocated. State and the W schedule are reused across blocks, and a fresh copy of H(0) is made per call so the function is pure/re-entrant.

CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE: ESM only; no require(, no module.exports; no node: builtin; no crypto in any spelling, no subtle/webcrypto/createHmac/createHash; no Buffer, no TextEncoder/TextDecoder. (`ArrayBuffer` appears as an ECMAScript global in an instanceof check and JSDoc — that is the standard global, not Node's Buffer; hmac.mjs uses it the same way. A naive substring grep for "Buffer" will hit it, a word-boundary grep will not.)

Plus RFC 4231 HMAC-SHA256 cases 1,2,3,4,6,7 through hmac.mjs (case 6/7 exercise the 131-byte key hash and a 216-byte message), a deterministic length sweep 0..200, an input-not-mutated check, and arithmetic checks of the 64-bit bit-length words for 2^29 and 600,000,000 byte lengths.

900 lines, ESM, zero npm/builtin deps. Only import is `import { utf8Decode } from './bytes.mjs'`. No require(/module.exports/crypto/Buffer/TextEncoder/TextDecoder/node: tokens anywhere (grep-verified). `node --check` clean.

REQUIRED-INTERFACE EXPORTS
- pyJsonDumpsCompact(value) -> string. Equals json.dumps(v, separators=(',',':')) with ensure_ascii=True. Raw only for 0x20..0x7e minus '"' and '\'; so '/', '<', '>', '&' stay raw and 0x7f becomes . Short escapes \b \t \n \f \r; everything else \uXXXX lowercase 4-digit. The loop walks UTF-16 code units, so astral chars emit the surrogate pair (U+1F600 -> 😀) and lone surrogates survive.
  Accepts: Map (preferred, order-preserving), plain object (Object.prototype/null proto only), Array, string, number, BigInt, PyFloat, boolean, null, undefined (-> null). Non-string dict keys coerced like Python (int/float/bool/None); anything else -> TypeError "keys must be str, int, float, bool or None, not X". Unsupported values -> TypeError "Object of type X is not JSON serializable". Cycles -> Error("Circular reference detected").
- pyJsonLoads(text) -> Map for objects (insertion-ordered; a repeated key updates in place like a Python dict), Array, string, number, boolean, null. Accepts a string OR UTF-8 bytes (Uint8Array/number[]), so it is safe if jwt.mjs passes jws payload bytes straight in. Also accepts the CPython default constants NaN/Infinity/-Infinity, and rejects a leading BOM like CPython. Malformed input throws the exported JSONDecodeError (subclass of Error, name 'JSONDecodeError', with .msg/.pos/.lineno/.colno) whose message is byte-identical to CPython, e.g. "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)", "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes", "Expecting ':' delimiter", "Expecting ',' delimiter", "Extra data", "Unterminated string starting at", "Invalid \escape", "Invalid \uXXXX escape", "Invalid control character at".
- isJsonInteger(value) -> true for any integral Number (Number.isInteger) and for BigInt; false for PyFloat markers, fractional/NaN/Infinite Numbers, and non-numbers.

FLOAT TAGGING (the design decision you asked me to document)
Minimal-wrapping marker class. Integers and fractional/NaN/Infinite floats are always plain primitives. The ONLY wrapped case is a JSON float literal whose value is integral ("1.0", "2e3", "-0.0"), because that is the only value where int-vs-float is not recoverable. Those return `new PyFloat(v)`, which exposes .value, valueOf() (arithmetic/comparison work), toString() -> Python repr ("1.0"), toJSON(). Integer literal "-0" is normalised to +0 since Python's int has no -0.
IMPORTANT INTEROP DETAIL: pyrepr.mjs was already written and its unwrapTaggedNumber() only recognises boxed Numbers or objects carrying __pyFloat===true / pyType==='float' / isFloat===true. So PyFloat instances also set all three of those tag fields — a PyFloat therefore reprs correctly through the existing pyRepr without pyrepr.mjs being touched. Verified: pyRepr(pyJsonLoads('{"a":1.0,"b":2e3,"c":1.5,"d":-0.0,"e":3,"f":-0,"g":1e16,"h":1e-7}')) is byte-identical to CPython's repr. For this program no float ever occurs (info is str, iat is int), so no marker is ever produced in practice.

EXTRA (non-contract) EXPORTS, free to ignore: isJsonFloat, jsonNumberValue (unwraps PyFloat/BigInt to a number), pythonFloatRepr (shortest round-trip digits, CPython's sci-vs-positional threshold decpt<=-4 || decpt>16, exponent signed and zero-padded to 2 -> "1e-07", "1e+16", "1000000000000000.0"), PyFloat, JSONDecodeError.

KNOWN, DELIBERATE LIMITATION: per the module contract integers come back as Numbers, so a JSON integer above 2**53-1 loses precision (123456789012345678901 -> ...683968) where CPython keeps an exact int. Unreachable for this program (iat ~1.7e9). Mitigation on the write side: an integral Number is always serialised as exact digits via BigInt, never "1e+21", so output stays valid JSON.

VERIFIED byte-identical to the reference executable across 87 curated + 360 fuzz differential cases (3 seeds, random code points over ASCII/BMP/all astral planes) plus 92 local unit cases.

ZERO imports — the file contains no import statement at all (the only two occurrences of the word "import" are prose in the header comment), so there is no cycle risk and no dependency on pyjson.mjs. No require(, no module.exports, no crypto/Buffer/TextEncoder references. 334 lines.

EXACT SEMANTICS IMPLEMENTED
- pyReprString mirrors CPython unicode_repr: quote = '"' iff the string contains ' and no "; otherwise "'" with ' backslash-escaped. Escape order is (1) enclosing quote or backslash, (2) 0x09/0x0a/0x0d -> \t/\n/\r, (3) cp < 0x20 || cp == 0x7f -> \xXX, (4) cp < 0x7f raw, (5) non-ASCII: raw if printable else \xXX (<=0xff) / \uXXXX (<=0xffff) / \UXXXXXXXX. Lowercase hex, iteration by code point via for..of.
- Printability: one cached /u RegExp '^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$'. U+0020 is force-printable via an ASCII fast path (cp<0x80 -> printable iff 0x20<=cp!=0x7f), which is REQUIRED because U+0020 does match \p{Zs}. Built lazily in try/catch; on failure it silently degrades to a static range table instead of throwing at import time (verified by patching the category to an invalid name: no throw, 91/92 still correct; only unassigned-Cn detection is lost, which a range table inherently cannot enumerate).
- pyRepr: Map -> dict via pyRepr(key) + ': ' + pyRepr(val) joined with ', ' ({} when empty); plain object -> dict via Object.entries; Array -> list; Set -> set() / {a, b}; boolean -> True/False; null AND undefined -> None; bigint -> decimal; boxed String/Boolean unwrapped.
- Numbers: integral Number primitives render as Python int (plain decimal; values >= 1e21 go through BigInt so they never come out exponential). Non-integral, and -0, render with Python float repr: shortest round-trip digits taken from toExponential(), exponential form iff decpt <= -4 || decpt > 16, exponent padded to >= 2 digits (1e-05, not 1e-5), always a '.' or 'e' (1.0), plus nan/inf/-inf and -0.0.

FLOAT TAGGING — CONFIRMED COMPATIBLE WITH pyjson.mjs AS WRITTEN
Because 1.0 and 1 are the same JS Number, an UNTAGGED integral primitive renders as int '1'. pyRepr recognises pyjson's PyFloat marker by duck-typing (no import): any object with a numeric .value plus __pyFloat === true, pyType === 'float', or isFloat === true renders as a float; __pyInt/pyType==='int'/isInteger render as int; boxed Number objects are treated as floats. The PyFloat class in the delivered /output/lib/pyjson.mjs sets all three tag fields and .value, so this matches exactly — verified live: pyRepr(pyJsonLoads('{"x":1.0}')) -> {'x': 1.0} while pyRepr(pyJsonLoads('{"x":1}')) -> {'x': 1}, and new PyFloat(1e16) -> 1e+16.

FOR THE INTEGRATOR
- decode() must return a Map (confirmed pyjson.mjs does) — pyRepr relies on it for insertion order; verified {'2': 'a', '1': 'b'} keeps order that a plain object would reorder.
- The exact target line reproduces: pyRepr(new Map([['info','iat_data_5'],['iat',1786341257]])) === "{'info': 'iat_data_5', 'iat': 1786341257}".
- Lone surrogates (from Python's argv surrogateescape on invalid UTF-8) render correctly: the executable prints {'info': 'bad\udcff\udcfeend'} and pyReprString produces the same, so whichever module decodes argv should pass lone surrogates through unchanged rather than substituting U+FFFD.
- Two inputs are untestable against the reference and are covered by unit test only: a NUL byte cannot pass through argv on POSIX, and lone surrogates cannot survive an argv UTF-8 round trip.

Only /output/lib/pyrepr.mjs was created; no other file under /output was touched. Scratch harness: /workspace/verify/pyrepr_selftest.mjs, pyrepr_difftest.sh, pyrepr_fuzztest.sh, pyrepr_integration.mjs, pyrepr_cases.mjs, pyrepr_fuzz_cases.mjs.

HOW test17.mjs MUST CALL IT (verified against the reference binary):

  import { ArgumentParser } from './lib/argparse.mjs';
  const parser = new ArgumentParser();                                   // prog defaults to 'test17_executable'
  parser.addArgument('--data', { type: 'str', required: true });
  parser.addArgument('--verify_iat', { type: 'str', required: true, choices: ['true', 'false'] });
  const args = parser.parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));                   // -> { data: string, verify_iat: string }

Namespace keys are argparse dest names: `args.data` and `args.verify_iat` (underscore preserved). The
auto-registered -h/--help action has a SUPPRESS default, so `help` is NOT a key on the namespace.
`parseArgs()` with no argument defaults to `process.argv.slice(2)` itself, so either form works.
IMPORTANT: register --data BEFORE --verify_iat — registration order drives the usage line, the help body
and the "the following arguments are required: --data, --verify_iat" ordering.

parseArgs never returns on the error/help paths: it writes to process.stderr / process.stdout and calls
process.exit(2) / process.exit(0). Callers need no try/catch.

Full public surface: constructor({ prog = 'test17_executable', addHelp = true, allowAbbrev = true }),
addArgument(optionStrings, { type, required, choices, help, dest, metavar, action, defaultValue, nargs }),
parseArgs(argv), parseKnownArgs(argv) -> [namespace, extras], formatUsage(), formatHelp(),
error(message), exitWithHelp(). `optionStrings` may be a string or an array. `type` accepts a function or
'str' | 'int' | 'float' (default identity/str). `action: 'help'` and `nargs: 0` are supported.
Positional arguments are deliberately rejected with a thrown Error — the ported script declares none, and
the whole "unrecognized arguments" / "--" model below depends on there being none.

FIDELITY NOTES (the reference is a PyInstaller bundle of CPython 3.12.5+; `-hx` printing help instead of
erroring pins the minor version, so the newer code paths were ported):
- _parse_optional / _get_option_tuples / _match_argument / _get_values / consume_optional are transcribed
  from that revision, including the `sep` handling added in 3.12.5.
- "--" is classified as pattern char '-' and everything after it as 'A'. Because nargs patterns for
  *optionals* have their '-' placeholders stripped, an option can never swallow "--": `--data -- x` gives
  "argument --data: expected one argument", while `--data=--` yields the literal string '--' (3.12.5+ only
  strips a leading "--" for positionals).
- Required-args check runs inside parse_known_args, so it is reported BEFORE "unrecognized arguments";
  invalid-choice / expected-one-argument / ignored-explicit-argument fire earlier still (during the parse
  loop); -h wins as soon as it is reached.
- Error text reproduced exactly: "the following arguments are required: --data, --verify_iat",
  "argument --verify_iat: invalid choice: 'TRUE' (choose from 'true', 'false')",
  "argument --data: expected one argument", "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'",
  "unrecognized arguments: -- extra", "ambiguous option: --=x could match --help, --data, --verify_iat".
- Help column geometry is computed generically (help_position = min(maxInvocation+2, 24)); actions with no
  help end immediately after the invocation with no trailing whitespace.

ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: terminal width is pinned to 80 columns (Python's shutil.get_terminal_size
fallback for a non-tty), so usage/help are never re-wrapped. The reference DOES re-wrap when COLUMNS is
exported (e.g. `COLUMNS=20 ./test17_executable --help` produces a 5-line usage block). Implementing
HelpFormatter's usage-wrapping algorithm was judged higher risk than value; with COLUMNS unset or >= 80 the
output is byte-identical.

DEPENDENCY: the single import is `{ pyReprString } from './pyrepr.mjs'` (used for %r quoting in the
invalid-choice / ignored-explicit-argument / invalid-type messages). It must be exported by the pyrepr agent
or the module will fail to load. No node: builtins, no crypto, no Buffer/TextEncoder, no require/module.exports.

VERIFICATION: 74 curated argv cases plus 1100 randomised argv permutations were diffed against
/workspace/dataset/test17_executable — identical exit code, identical stderr bytes, identical stdout bytes on
the --help paths, identical parsed --data value on the success paths (0 failures). Scratch harness lives in

pyrepr.mjs stub and argparse-driver.mjs). Nothing else under /output was created or modified.

/output/test17.mjs is the entry point and intentionally exports NOTHING — like the Python script it is a top-level side-effecting program. It is the only file I created under /output; nothing else was touched.

Verified against the real module already on disk.

KEY DECISIONS
- The claim set is a `new Map([['info', args.data], ['iat', pyInt(timeTime())]])`, not an object literal, so insertion order survives into both the payload JSON and the dict repr.
- `prog` is pinned to 'test17_executable' rather than derived from argv[1], so usage/help/error bytes match the reference no matter how the file is invoked.
- Guard uses `process.exitCode = 1` instead of `process.exit(1)`. This matters: `process.exit()` truncates pending async stdout writes on a pipe, which would swallow the already-printed token line. Confirmed by piping through `cat` — token line survives, stderr gets the exception, status is 1.
- Uncaught errors are rendered as CPython's final traceback line: `jose.exceptions.<Name>: <message>` for JOSEError subclasses, bare `<Name>: <message>` for builtins (e.g. a ValueError out of pyInt), and just `<Name>` when the message is empty. The traceback frames are deliberately not faked. Nothing on the success path is caught.
- Both original Chinese comments are preserved on their corresponding lines (`// issued at (iat) claim记录token的发行时间` above `secret`, `// 根据参数决定是否验证iat` above `verifyIat`).
